title: Building TriageNet — When Algorithms Meet Healthcare
content:
My most complex project yet just hit a major milestone. TriageNet is an 
AI-powered hospital triage and resource optimization system I'm building 
as my final year project at AEC — and it's unlike anything I've built before.

The idea: connect 4 regional hospitals in a weighted graph network, then 
use algorithms to automatically route patients to the right facility in 
real time. Not just the nearest hospital — the one with the right beds, 
the right equipment, and the right specialist available. All three 
conditions have to match before any assignment happens.

Under the hood: a Logistic Regression ML model scores patient severity 
from 0–100 using clinical vitals (SpO₂, heart rate, blood pressure, 
temperature, respiratory rate, age). Dijkstra's algorithm finds the 
shortest-path referral route. The Hungarian algorithm handles optimal 
bed assignment. And if SpO₂ drops below 90% with HR above 110 bpm, the 
system fires a sepsis early warning automatically.

Phase 1 and 2 are done — all 12 operational dashboard pages are live, 
the ML engine is running, and the Spring Boot backend with JWT auth and 
Docker Compose is scaffolded. Now comes the hardest part: wiring the 
backend algorithms to the frontend in real time.

This one's going to the final year presentation. Building it in public.
